title: Setting Recently Withdrawn Money Against the Surplus
content:
Money that has recently left an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is set against the surplus within a ceiling. The figure read is the total of withdrawals posted to the account in the one calendar month ending on the instruction date.

Where at least 2000.00 USD of withdrawals posted in that window, the surplus is reduced by those withdrawals up to a ceiling of 1000.00 USD, and never below zero.

Where at least 500.00 USD but less than 2000.00 USD of withdrawals posted in that window, the surplus is reduced by those withdrawals up to a ceiling of 400.00 USD, and never below zero.

Where less than 500.00 USD of withdrawals posted in that window, no withdrawal already posted is set against the surplus.

### Worked cases on a hypothetical surplus

Take a surplus of 6000.00 USD.

| Withdrawals in the one calendar month ending on the instruction date | Reduction | Surplus after the reduction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5000.00 USD | 1000.00 USD, the ceiling of the first rule | 5000.00 USD |
| 2000.00 USD | 1000.00 USD, the ceiling of the first rule | 5000.00 USD |
| 900.00 USD | 400.00 USD, the ceiling of the second rule | 5600.00 USD |
| 500.00 USD | 400.00 USD, the ceiling of the second rule | 5600.00 USD |
| 300.00 USD | none | 6000.00 USD |

The ceiling caps the reduction rather than the withdrawals: where the withdrawals fall below the ceiling, the reduction is the withdrawals themselves. Where the surplus is smaller than the reduction, the reduced figure is held at zero rather than going below it.

### Boundary of the figures

Withdrawals of exactly 2000.00 USD fall under the first rule, exactly 500.00 USD under the second, and 499.99 USD under the third.
